messages.content: We are ready to start on the longer September vacation. I had mentioned St. Simons, but after looking at the drive and the beaches, make the comparison Amelia Island versus Hilton Head instead. The dates are fixed: Saturday, September 12 through Saturday, September 19, 2026. One room for my wife and me.

I’ll compare Amelia Island and Hilton Head for seven nights, September 12-19, for two adults in one room. What ceiling should I use for the complete hotel cost, including taxes and mandatory resort or destination fees?
Keep the full stay at or below $2,650. Parking should be included in the total if the hotel charges for it, since we will be driving from Atlanta.

Understood. I’ll use $2,650 as the all-in lodging ceiling and count seven nights, taxes, required fees, and one vehicle. I found representative availability in both destinations, but the tradeoff is fairly sharp: Amelia has a beachfront option within budget, while comparable direct-beach Hilton Head rooms are above it.
Show me the clearest comparison. I do not need a huge list yet.

For Amelia Island, Surf & Sand Amelia has a standard room available for all seven nights at an average base rate of $279. The room subtotal is $1,953, taxes are $234.36, the resort fee is $245, and self-parking is $70. Complete stay: $2,502.36. The property opens directly onto the beach.

For Hilton Head, Shoreline Resort Hilton Head has a standard room available at an average base rate of $319. The room subtotal is $2,233, taxes are $245.63, the resort fee is $315, and parking is $140. Complete stay: $2,933.63. It also has direct beach access.
So Amelia is $147.64 under the ceiling, and the Hilton Head one is $283.63 over. Is that right?
Yes. Those differences are correct based on the complete totals: Amelia is $147.64 under $2,650, and the direct-beach Hilton Head option is $283.63 over.
Is Hilton Head generally that much higher for this week, or did you just happen to pick an expensive resort?

The beachfront inventory I checked on Hilton Head is consistently higher for those dates. Two other direct-beach properties total $3,087.42 and $3,264.18 after required fees, tax, and parking. There is a lower-cost Hilton Head option, Harbor Dunes Inn, at $2,574.91 complete, but it is not beachfront.
How far is Harbor Dunes from the sand? I care more about whether getting to the beach is simple than whether the hotel can technically call itself oceanfront.

Harbor Dunes is about 0.4 mile from the nearest public beach access, roughly an 8- to 10-minute walk. The route is mostly along a sidewalk, then across one signalized intersection. The hotel does not provide a shuttle. Its complete total is $2,574.91: $1,995 room subtotal, $219.45 tax, $220 required destination fee, and $140 parking.
That is a real alternative. What does Amelia look like if we compare a walk-to-beach hotel rather than the one directly on the beach?

Seaside Courtyard Amelia is available for the full week and sits about 0.3 mile from a public beach entrance, approximately a 6- to 8-minute walk with one road crossing. Its complete total is $2,214.08: $1,827 room subtotal, $219.24 tax, a $97.84 required fee, and $70 parking. That is $288.28 less than Surf & Sand Amelia.
For the $288 difference, I would keep Surf & Sand in the Amelia comparison. Walking is acceptable, but having the beach right there is worth that amount over a full week.

That leaves two useful finalists: Surf & Sand Amelia at $2,502.36 with direct beach access, and Harbor Dunes Hilton Head at $2,574.91 with an 8- to 10-minute walk. Both are within the $2,650 ceiling, and the difference between them is $72.55.
Before choosing a destination, are those totals actually bookable now for every night, or are they estimates assembled from advertised rates?

They are current seven-night quotes with continuous availability for September 12-19. Each total uses the rate shown for the selected room across all seven nights rather than multiplying the lowest advertised nightly rate. Neither quote is being held, so price and inventory can change before booking.
What are the cancellation terms on the two finalists? Just for this comparison; I am not ready to reserve tonight.

Surf & Sand Amelia allows cancellation without penalty through 6:00 p.m. local time on September 9. After that, the penalty is one night plus tax. Harbor Dunes Hilton Head allows free cancellation through 11:59 p.m. local time on September 7; after the deadline, the full stay becomes nonrefundable. No charge is due now for either flexible quote.

The Amelia option looks stronger. We get direct access, it costs less, and its late-cancellation exposure is smaller. Still, I want the focused search to follow one rule rather than drifting into luxury resorts we will not book.
What rule should I use when I narrow the Amelia Island results?

For our coastal vacations, preserve straightforward beach access, ideally on the beach or close enough to walk, while keeping the complete hotel stay within the budget I give you. Do not trade away practical beach access just to surface a cheaper inland room.

I’ll apply that to the next search: Amelia Island, September 12-19, one room for two adults, with direct or walkable beach access and a complete total no higher than $2,650 including taxes, required fees, and parking. Surf & Sand Amelia is the current benchmark at $2,502.36, but nothing has been booked or held.
